title: Cy Twombly: Marocco 1952/1953

description.main: Photographs from Cy Twombly's 1952-53 journey through Morocco with Robert Rauschenberg, published for the 2023 exhibition at the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech. Texts by Tina Barouti, Anne-Grit Becker and Natalie Dupêcher, in Italian and English.
description.extended:
Published for the 2023 exhibition at the Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech, this volume gathers photographs from the journey Cy Twombly made through Morocco with Robert Rauschenberg in 1952–53.

Twombly left New York in the fall of 1952 on a travelling scholarship from the Virginia Museum of Fine Arts. He met Rauschenberg in Casablanca, and the two went on to Marrakech, the Atlas Mountains and Tangier, then visited Paul Bowles in Tétouan. The pictures were taken with a Rolleiflex the two artists shared. They are kept with the sketches from the trip in the archives of the Cy Twombly Foundation and the Fondazione Nicola Del Roscio. The texts are by Tina Barouti, Anne-Grit Becker and Natalie Dupêcher. The book is in Italian and English and co-published by Humboldt Books and Éditions Jardin Majorelle.

Twombly is better known for his attachment to classical antiquity, and the trip records the interest he took at twenty-five in the Amazigh cultures of Morocco. Back in Rome in February 1953 he sketched ethnographic objects in the Museo Pigorini, drawings that survive as the North African Sketchbooks. Later that year he and Rauschenberg showed at the Stable Gallery in New York, where Twombly's paintings carried the names of Moroccan towns.
description.artist_bio: Cy Twombly (Lexington, Virginia, 1928 - Rome, 2011), an American artist known for his attachment to classical antiquity.
description.exhibition_context: Cy Twombly, Morocco, 1952/1953, curated by Nicola Del Roscio, Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech, March 4 to July 2, 2023, mounted by the Fondation Jardin Majorelle with the Cy Twombly Foundation and the Fondazione Nicola Del Roscio.
